newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end firm on debt buyback talk.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end firm on debt buyback talk.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed modestly higher Monday, extending their recent winning streak and setting a third consecutive five-year high.

"Stocks were boosted first by the drop in U.S. long bond yields early this morning and then by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez's comments on a possible debt buyback this year, which should continue to attract buyers tomorrow," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index closed up 0.4 percent at 841.69, slipping off a session high of 848.74. The MerVal had gained 3.5 percent last week.
"Even though Wall Street pulled back today we stayed firm. In fact the MerVal might pierce resistance at 850 thanks to the debt buyback factor," Daneri said.

Floor volume picked up to 36.6 million pesos from a token 17.8 million traded Friday during the U.S. Independence Day holiday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 152.5 million pesos from 113.1 million pesos Friday.

"The AFJPs (private pension funds) were active today and in general the market should stay firm, latching onto the news of a possible debt buyback and to the drop in U.S. long bond yields," another dealer said.
The broad market index closed up 0.5 percent, with winners beating losers 44 to 20 and 22 issues closing unchanged.
The best main-tier performers were holding company Garovaglio, which jumped 4.7 percent, and pulp and paper maker Celulosa and Banco Frances, both up 3.7 percent.

MerVal losers were led by cement firm Polledo, which dropped 2.5 percent, electricity generator Central Costanera, down 2.0 percent, and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur and carmaker Ciadea, both off 1.2 percent.
